papers.title: Genome-resolved analysis reveals disruption of gut microbial vitamin B and K2 biosynthesis during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii infection remodels the gut microbiome, yet its impact on microbial vitamin biosynthetic potential and host redox metabolism remains unclear. Here, we integrated mouse gut metagenomes with publicly available metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to construct a genome-resolved atlas of B-vitamin and vitamin K2 biosynthesis. From 45,697 MAGs, we curated 4,771 representative genomes, of which 2,682 met high-quality criteria (completeness ≥90%, contamination <5%). Functional annotation identified 229,717 vitamin-related genes corresponding to 177 Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Geno
papers.summary: This study uses genome-resolved metagenomics to show that Toxoplasma gondii infection disrupts gut microbial biosynthesis of B vitamins and vitamin K2 in mice. By curating high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes, the authors built a functional atlas of vitamin biosynthesis genes and linked infection-driven microbiome shifts to altered vitamin production potential.

papers.title: ON-Time enables rapid microbiome sequencing and analysis for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Clinical application of microbiome-guided therapies in the intensive care unit (ICU) requires a method to rapidly analyze patient microbiomes to guide urgent treatment decisions. Conventional microbiome sequencing and analysis methods require long turnaround times, methodological complexity, and high costs that are barriers to clinical application. Here, we describe a method for rapid (<5 h turnaround from sample to results) and accurate metagenomic sequencing and taxonomic analysis of microbiomes in individual patient fecal samples, called ON-Time. ON-Time uses a simplified and rapid wet-lab
papers.summary: This paper introduces ON-Time, a rapid (<5 hours) and accurate metagenomic sequencing and analysis method for individual patient fecal samples, designed for clinical use in the ICU to guide urgent microbiome-based treatment decisions. It overcomes the long turnaround times, complexity, and high costs of conventional methods, enabling timely precision medicine applications.

papers.title: Large-scale benchmarking of prokaryotic annotation tools across thousands of species.
papers.abstract: Genome annotation is an important step in deriving functional meaning from prokaryotic sequencing data, yet systematic evaluations guiding tool selection are lacking. We present the first large-scale investigation of four prominent open-source annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes. This includes Escherichia coli strains for baseline performance, thousands of archaea and bacteria genomes, as well as frameshifted and metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.summary: This study provides the first large-scale benchmarking of four major prokaryotic genome annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across over 156,000 diverse genomes, including bacteria, archaea, and metagenome-assembled genomes. The findings offer systematic guidance on tool selection by comparing performance on baseline and challenging datasets, filling a critical gap in the field.

papers.title: Exploring the ecological drivers of bacteriophage diversity and functional viral potential in the skin of the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages play important roles in shaping microbial community dynamics across diverse environments. In the amphibian skin, most microbiome studies have focused on bacteria and their interactions with the fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), leaving other microbial components, including viruses, largely unexplored. Here, we present the first characterization of the viral community in the amphibian skin microbiome, focusing on ecological drivers of bacteriophage diversity and functional potential in the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani. Using public shotgun metagenomes, we found that the
papers.summary: This study provides the first characterization of bacteriophage communities on amphibian skin, using public shotgun metagenomes from the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani. It identifies ecological drivers of phage diversity and functional potential, highlighting the previously overlooked viral component of the amphibian skin microbiome.

papers.title: Meta-CD: a metagenomic sequencing coverage and depth calculator for target species.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic Coverage and Depth Calculator (Meta-CD) is a convenient, biologist-friendly tool for determining coverage and depth to enhance taxonomic detection, functional profiling, and metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) recovery in metagenomics. It supports experimental design and post-sequencing analysis, modeling how genome size, relative abundance, sequencing depth, and DNA quantity influence detection of target species.
papers.summary: Meta-CD is a user-friendly tool that calculates sequencing coverage and depth for target species in metagenomics projects. It helps researchers plan experiments and analyze post-sequencing data by modeling how factors like genome size, abundance, and sequencing depth affect detection of specific organisms.

papers.title: Proteo-metabolomic integration identifies stage-specific candidate biomarkers for Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with a prolonged prodromal phase and complex motor symptoms. Despite improved clinical criteria, early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring remain challenging. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma metabolites and proteins show biomarker potential, their utility in predictive models is insufficiently characterized. We employed a secondary computational approach to integrate proteometabolomic profiles from CSF and plasma samples of >1100 Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) participants. Using multi-omics ma
papers.summary: This study integrates proteomic and metabolomic data from over 1,100 Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative participants to identify stage-specific candidate biomarkers for Parkinson's disease. The multi-omics approach reveals distinct molecular signatures associated with different disease stages, potentially improving early diagnosis and disease monitoring.

papers.title: Microbial content versus microbial interaction: the impact of medications on CF airway microbial ecosystems.
papers.abstract: The airways of people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) are often colonized by a variety of different microbes. Although much effort has been put into cataloguing the impact of medication on the identities and abundances of these microbes, far less has been directed towards examining this from an ecological perspective, i.e., examining how medications affect the network and types of interactions between microbes.
papers.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
papers.summary: This review highlights a gap in cystic fibrosis research: most studies catalog how medications alter the types and abundances of airway microbes, but few examine how drugs affect the ecological interactions (networks) between these microbes. The authors argue for a shift toward studying microbial interaction networks to better understand treatment effects on the airway ecosystem.

papers.title: The cystic fibrosis gut microbial dysbiosis index (CF-GMDI): a quantitative measure of gut microbial imbalance in children with cystic fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Gut dysbiosis is a hallmark of cystic fibrosis (CF), typically characterised using non-specific diversity metrics and study-specific taxonomic lists, limiting comparability across studies. We aimed to develop a metagenomic, species-level CF Gut Microbial Dysbiosis Index (CF-GMDI) to standardise measurement of gut microbial imbalance in children with CF (cwCF) METHODS: CF-GMDI was derived using stool metagenomic data from the PEARL-CF study (70 cwCF; 67 healthy controls (HC); 0-6 years). Differentially abundant taxa were identified between cwCF and HC using MaAsLin2. The index was calculated as
papers.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
papers.summary: The authors developed a metagenomic, species-level CF Gut Microbial Dysbiosis Index (CF-GMDI) to standardize measurement of gut microbial imbalance in children with cystic fibrosis. Using stool metagenomic data from the PEARL-CF study, they identified differentially abundant taxa and constructed an index that quantifies dysbiosis, potentially improving comparability across studies.

papers.title: Optimizing a culture-enriched hybrid metagenomics pipeline to assess the AMR footprint of livestock manure in anaerobic digestate.
papers.abstract: The role of environmental samples from livestock production systems, including manure and anaerobic digestate, as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) is likely underestimated because conventional metagenomic approaches can overlook low-abundance ARGs and often lack the resolution to associate these genes with their microbial hosts and co-localized mobile genetic elements (MGEs). We evaluated whether culture-enriched metagenomics (CEMG), with and without antibiotic selection, enhances ARG detection in anaerobic digestate and improves the resolution of ARG-MGE-host associations u
papers.summary: This study evaluates a culture-enriched metagenomics (CEMG) pipeline, with and without antibiotic selection, for detecting antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in livestock manure and anaerobic digestate. The approach improves detection of low-abundance ARGs and provides better resolution of ARG associations with microbial hosts and mobile genetic elements compared to conventional metagenomics.

papers.title: Unveiling the mechanism of metabolites derived from gut microbiota in the treatment of acute kidney injury via network pharmacology and bioinformatics.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects a considerable proportion of patients that represents a major challenge for clinical treatment. Gut microbiota metabolites have been reported to attenuate acute kidney injury (AKI), yet their underlying mechanisms remain largely elusive. The present study aimed to explore the protective mechanisms of these metabolites against AKI using.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and bioinformatics to investigate how gut microbiota metabolites protect against acute kidney injury (AKI), aiming to uncover the underlying molecular mechanisms. The findings provide a systems-level view of the metabolite-target-pathway network, potentially informing new therapeutic strategies for AKI.

papers.title: A Critical Synthesis of Machine Learning in Autism Spectrum Disorder Genomic Research: From Transcriptomics to Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent impairments in social communication, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors. This narrative review synthesizes advances in machine learning applications to ASD genomic research through May 2026, spanning gene expression analysis, whole-exome sequencing (WES), non-coding variant interpretation, multi-omics integration, single-cell transcriptomics, epigenetic profiling, and gut microbiome analysis. A purposive, thematic literature synthesis approach was employed, allowing broad coverage o
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes recent advances in applying machine learning to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) genomic research, covering areas such as gene expression, whole-exome sequencing, non-coding variants, multi-omics integration, single-cell transcriptomics, epigenetics, and the gut microbiome. It provides a broad overview of how ML methods are being used to identify ASD-related patterns and biomarkers across diverse data types.

papers.title: Convergent methodologies in prosthetic joint infection research: integrating transdisciplinary approaches to understand and prevent biofilm-driven failure of orthopaedic prostheses.
papers.abstract: Prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) remain among the most devastating complications of arthroplasty, imposing substantial clinical, economic and patient burdens. Although culture-based diagnostics underpin current clinical practice, PJIs are biofilm-driven infections shaped by taxonomic diversity, spatial organization, host responses and surface interactions, meaning conventional approaches provide only a partial and often decontextualized view of the infection process. We examine how convergent methodologies can transform PJI research by integrating approaches that have traditionally been stud
papers.summary: This review argues that prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) are complex, biofilm-driven diseases that cannot be fully understood through conventional culture-based diagnostics alone. It advocates for integrating transdisciplinary approaches—such as genomics, spatial biology, and host-response analysis—to gain a more complete picture of infection mechanisms and to develop better prevention and treatment strategies.

papers.title: Benchmarking methods for extracting microbial signal from host-dominated metatranscriptomes.
papers.abstract: Human RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data originally generated for human transcriptome profiling are overwhelmingly dominated by host sequences, yet they often contain a small fraction of non-human reads that can be exploited for microbial detection. When such datasets are repurposed for secondary microbiome-oriented analyses, extracting and accurately classifying this weak microbial signal becomes technically challenging, and no ready-to-use pipeline currently exists. In this study, we evaluate computational strategies for filtering host reads and classifying microbial transcripts in host-dominated
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational methods for extracting and classifying weak microbial signals from host-dominated human RNA-seq data, addressing the lack of a ready-to-use pipeline for repurposing such datasets for microbiome analysis. It evaluates host read filtering and microbial transcript classification strategies, providing guidance for researchers working with host-contaminated metatranscriptomes.

papers.title: Maternal secretor status and human milk oligosaccharides influence the infant gut resistome.
papers.abstract: The infant gut resistome is established early in life and is shaped by perinatal exposures, yet the mechanisms underlying its modulation remain unclear. We combined shotgun metagenomics of fecal samples from 57 one-month-old infants and paired milk samples from 50 mothers in the MAMI cohort to investigate the influence of maternal secretor status on early-life resistome development. Longitudinal follow-up at 6 and 12 months, and also further validation in the independent Lifelines NEXT (LLNEXT) cohort, support our findings. Cesarean section (C-section) was associated with increased antibiotic
papers.summary: This study investigates how maternal secretor status and human milk oligosaccharides shape the infant gut resistome. Using metagenomic data from the MAMI cohort and validation in an independent cohort, the authors find that C-section is associated with increased antibiotic resistance gene abundance, while maternal secretor status and milk oligosaccharides modulate the resistome, suggesting potential dietary strategies to reduce antibiotic resistance carriage in infants.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of microbial communities, assembly processes, and life-history strategies in a mariculture-impacted eutrophic bay and adjacent coastal sediments.
papers.abstract: Coastal embayments are increasingly subjected to intensive mariculture, which delivers sustained nutrient, organic matter, and antibiotics to sediments, yet microbiome responses remain poorly understood. Here we compared sediment microbiomes of the eutrophic Xiangshan Bay (XSB) and oligotrophic East China Sea (ECS), integrating cell counts, 16S rRNA amplicon, metagenomics, and cultivation-based resistance assays. Cell counts and amplicon data showed that XSB harbored higher microbial abundance (1.28 ×108-1.34 ×109 vs. 2.07 ×107-4.43 ×108 cells g⁻¹), Chao1 richness (10,374-16,674 vs. 8311-12,28
papers.summary: This study compares sediment microbiomes between a mariculture-impacted eutrophic bay and an oligotrophic coastal sea, finding that eutrophic sediments harbor higher microbial abundance and diversity. The authors integrate amplicon, metagenomic, and cultivation data to reveal distinct community assembly processes and life-history strategies, with eutrophic conditions favoring copiotrophic taxa and increased antibiotic resistance. These findings highlight how intensive mariculture reshapes benthic microbial communities and their functional potential.

papers.title: Syndromic cholera diagnosis masks diverse causes of diarrhoeal disease in Burundi revealed by portable metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Cholera outbreaks remain a major public-health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, where diagnostic capacity is limited and clinical case definitions are non-specific and re ly heavily on syndromic diagnosis. Rapid identification of Vibrio cholerae is critical, yet cholera-suspected diarrhoea can have multiple infectious causes not captured by targeted diagnostics.
papers.summary: This study uses portable metagenomics to analyze diarrheal samples from cholera-suspected patients in Burundi, revealing that many cases are caused by pathogens other than Vibrio cholerae. The findings highlight the limitations of syndromic diagnosis and the value of metagenomic sequencing for accurate pathogen identification in outbreak settings.

papers.title: xoxF-linked methanol oxidation signals recur across wetland metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Wetlands are globally important methane-cycling ecosystems, but methanol oxidation remains less frequently emphasized than methane oxidation in community-level metagenomic analyses. Recent studies have highlighted the ecological importance of the lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase XoxF, yet wetland-focused xoxF literature remains comparatively limited relative to marine, freshwater, and other environmental systems. Here, we screened wetland-associated records in IMG/M using methane-metabolism and enzyme-centered queries focused on EC 1.1.2.10/xoxF and related methanol-oxidation annota
papers.summary: This study screens wetland metagenomes from IMG/M and finds that lanthanide-dependent methanol oxidation genes (xoxF) are widespread and recurrent across diverse wetland ecosystems, highlighting their overlooked ecological role in methane-cycling communities. The work underscores the importance of including methanol oxidation in wetland microbial analyses.

papers.title: Rumen DNA virome plasticity and viral metabolic potential are associated with seasonal adaptation in grazing yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
papers.abstract: As a diverse and abundant component of the rumen ecosystem, viruses interact with other microorganisms and are thought to influence microbial metabolism and host productivity. However, how the rumen virome responds to seasonal fluctuations in extreme environments remains poorly understood. Here, metagenomic analyses were used to investigate temporal dynamics of viral diversity, functional potential, and virus-host associations in the rumen virome of yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau across warm and cold seasons.
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to characterize how the rumen virome of grazing yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau changes between warm and cold seasons, revealing seasonal plasticity in viral diversity and functional potential. The findings suggest that viruses may help microbial communities adapt to extreme environmental fluctuations, potentially influencing host metabolism and productivity.

papers.title: Decadal Resampling Reveals Widespread Increases in Soil Microbial Diversity Associated With Nitrogen Deposition.
papers.abstract: Simulated manipulation experiments, such as nitrogen addition to mimic atmospheric nitrogen deposition, are widely used in global change research. However, experimental manipulations may differ from real-world environmental change in their intensity, duration, and co-occurrence, leaving long-term changes in soil microbial communities and soil health insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we resampled soils from 38 forest and grassland ecosystems across eastern China in 2009 and 2019 and assessed microbial taxonomic and functional diversity using shotgun metagenomics. Microbial diversi
papers.summary: By resampling soils from 38 forest and grassland sites across eastern China a decade apart, this study found that soil microbial diversity increased over time, likely driven by nitrogen deposition. The findings highlight that real-world environmental changes can have different effects on soil microbial communities than short-term experimental nitrogen additions.

papers.title: Major Depressive Disorder Signatures: A Review of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Powered Insights Into Gut Dysbiosis.
papers.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a highly common neuropsychiatric disorder globally. A variety of factors contribute to the neuropathology of MDD. Microbiome research in neuropsychiatric disorders such as MDD has recently attracted attention. Indeed, the gut-brain axis could influence the course of MDD through metabolites such as Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA), Quinolinate, and other factors. Such metabolites may modulate the balance of excitatory and inhibitory signals. Moreover, MDD features abundant hyperinflammatory bacteria, whereas anti-inflammatory butyrate-synthesizing genera are dec
papers.summary: This review explores how artificial intelligence (AI) is being used to analyze gut microbiome data in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), highlighting links between gut dysbiosis and the condition. It discusses how microbial metabolites like GABA and quinolinate may influence brain signaling and inflammation, and how AI can help identify disease signatures. The paper underscores the potential of AI-powered microbiome analysis for advancing understanding and diagnosis of MDD.

papers.title: A Narrative Review of Airway and Gut Microbiota in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Clinical Associations, Methodological Heterogeneity, and Translational Priorities.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous disorder in which exacerbation susceptibility, persistent inflammation, disease progression, and treatment response are not fully explained by spirometry. Culture-independent studies have associated airway and gut microbial features with clinically relevant COPD phenotypes, but findings are highly sensitive to sampling site, low biomass, contamination control, sequencing depth and platform, bioinformatic workflow, microbial-load quantification, medication exposure, disease state, and host or environmental confounding. Methodologic
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how airway and gut microbiota relate to COPD clinical features, highlighting that findings are highly variable due to methodological differences such as sampling site, sequencing platforms, and confounding factors. It emphasizes the need for standardized approaches and identifies translational priorities for microbiome-based diagnostics or therapies in COPD.

papers.title: Modulatory Effect of the Alfalfa Polysaccharide Fraction II on Cyclophosphamide-Induced Immunosuppression in Mice.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the protective effects of alfalfa polysaccharide fraction II (APS-II) on immunosuppression induced by cyclophosphamide (CTX) in mice. APS-II was extracted using ultrasound-assisted enzymatic extraction method and purified by DEAE-52 cellulose chromatography. Its structural characteristics, including molecular weight (Mw), monosaccharide composition, and thermal stability, were analyzed. A CTX-induced immunosuppressed mouse model was established to evaluate the effects of APS-II on immune organ indices, serum cytokines, antioxidant indicators in liver and spleen tissues,
papers.summary: This study examines whether alfalfa polysaccharide fraction II (APS-II) can protect against cyclophosphamide-induced immunosuppression in mice. The authors extracted and characterized APS-II, then showed it improved immune organ indices, serum cytokines, and antioxidant status in a mouse model, suggesting a potential immunomodulatory role.

papers.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Successful Multiparametric Microbiota Flow Cytometry.
papers.abstract: The role of the human microbiota in host health is an important area of research. Conventional characterization of the complex microbial communities colonizing the human body is primarily performed using culture-based or high-throughput sequencing approaches, which have improved general understanding yet lack cellular features relevant for interaction and function at the single-cell level. Flow cytometry is an established tool for single-cell analysis, and recent improvements, such as increased resolution of small cells and particles, offer possibilities for characterizing complex microbial co
papers.summary: This paper provides a practical, step-by-step protocol for using multiparametric flow cytometry to analyze complex microbial communities at the single-cell level, addressing limitations of culture-based and sequencing methods. It highlights recent technical improvements that enable high-resolution characterization of small microbial cells, offering a valuable resource for researchers studying microbiota-host interactions.

papers.title: Soil microbial effects on tree seedling performance during forest secondary succession.
papers.abstract: Soil microbiota influence seedling survival and abundance in mature forests. However, their role in tree species turnover during secondary forest succession remains unclear, especially in species-rich tropical forests. We conducted a shade house experiment to assess variation in the direction and strength of net soil microbial effects on seedling emergence, biomass growth, and mortality of seven tree species. We tested for effects of soil successional stage (0, 15, 25, and 115 years of forest recovery), tree species' association with successional stages (home stages where species peak in abund
papers.summary: This study experimentally tested how soil microbes from different forest successional stages affect the emergence, growth, and survival of seven tropical tree species. The findings reveal that soil microbial effects vary by successional stage and tree species, suggesting that soil microbiota play a role in driving tree species turnover during secondary forest succession.

papers.title: AResKGLM: a graph-grounded language-model framework for interpretable multi-hop antimicrobial resistance reasoning.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens microbiology and microbiome bioinformatics because resistance phenotypes are shaped by interactions among genes, mobile genetic elements, and functional environments across microbial communities. Prioritizing resistance determinants requires models that reason across knowledge graphs (KGs) linking genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes. Existing graph-based methods compress this evidence into scalar scores, whereas large language models can produce explanations not grounded in structured evidence. We developed AResKGLM (Antimicrobial
papers.summary: AResKGLM is a new framework that combines knowledge graphs with large language models to provide interpretable, multi-hop reasoning for antimicrobial resistance (AMR). It addresses the limitation of existing graph-based methods that output scalar scores and LLMs that lack structured grounding, enabling evidence-based explanations of resistance determinants.

papers.title: The Calcidiscus leptoporus genome reveals vitamin-mediated holobiont interactions.
papers.abstract: Coccolithophores are major marine phytoplankton that contribute to ocean carbon cycling through both organic carbon fixation and calcium carbonate biomineralization, yet the functional basis of their interactions with phycosphere bacteria remains poorly resolved. Here, we present the nuclear genome of the haploid phase of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus, a coccolithophore that calcifies in both life-cycle stages. We combined host genome analysis, genome-resolved characterization of associated bacteria, and a four-month vitamin-manipulation experiment to test how B-vitamin biosynthet
papers.summary: This study presents the nuclear genome of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus and combines it with metagenomic and experimental approaches to reveal that interactions with phycosphere bacteria are mediated by B-vitamin exchange, highlighting a vitamin-based holobiont mechanism in marine phytoplankton.

papers.title: Metagenome-scale modeling to assess microbiome metabolic complementarity for precision microbiota transplantation therapies.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) holds therapeutic promise beyond recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, but clinical outcomes remain unpredictable and donor-selection strategies remain limited, in part because the role of donor‒recipient metabolic interactions in shaping the post-FMT community remains poorly understood. Here, we leverage metagenome-scale metabolic modeling to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient microbiomes and predict post-FMT community composition. Using MICOM-derived metabolic models, we show that donor genomes whose metabolic f
papers.summary: This study uses metagenome-scale metabolic modeling to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient microbiomes, aiming to improve donor selection for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). The authors demonstrate that donor genomes with higher metabolic complementarity to the recipient's microbiome better predict post-FMT community composition, offering a potential precision approach to FMT therapies.

papers.title: Determinants of enteric hyperoxaluria in the SAMP1/YitFc mouse model of spontaneous ileitis.
papers.abstract: Enteric hyperoxaluria (EH) results from increased oxalate bioavailability in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, often affecting patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We investigated the pathophysiology of EH in an ileitis mouse model, hypothesizing that fat malabsorption, increased gut permeability, and microbial shifts collectively contribute to the hyperoxaluric phenotype in the setting of GI tract inflammation. SAMP1/YitFc (SAMP1) mice and their parental AKR controls were fed one of three diets varying in fat content (10%, 45%, or 60% kcal), each supplemented with 1% oxalate, for 6
papers.summary: This study uses the SAMP1/YitFc mouse model of spontaneous ileitis to investigate the mechanisms underlying enteric hyperoxaluria, a complication of inflammatory bowel disease. The authors test the hypothesis that fat malabsorption, increased gut permeability, and microbial shifts collectively contribute to hyperoxaluria, and they examine the effects of varying dietary fat content on the hyperoxaluric phenotype.

papers.title: Longitudinal development of infant oral ecosystem: salivary metabolomic, bacteriome, and virome dynamics in early infancy.
papers.abstract: This prospective cohort study investigated the longitudinal development of the salivary bacteriome, virome, and metabolome during early infancy. We assessed the associations between oral bacteria, viruses, and metabolites from 10 mother-infant dyads, with oral samples collected at 1 and 2 years of age. Forty saliva and plaque samples underwent untargeted metabolomic analysis, and infant saliva samples underwent metagenomic sequencing. Maternal salivary and plaque metabolomic profiles remained largely stable, whereas infant profiles were clearly separated from maternal profiles and changed with
papers.summary: This study tracks how the infant oral ecosystem—including bacteria, viruses, and metabolites—develops between ages 1 and 2, showing that infant profiles are distinct from their mothers' and evolve over time. The findings highlight coordinated changes across the salivary microbiome and metabolome during early childhood.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Mock Communities as Quality Control Materials for Clinical Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables comprehensive detection of a broad spectrum of microorganisms. However, its clinical application faces two major challenges: the development of appropriate microbiome-based biomarkers and the need to ensure the reproducibility and quality of the microbiome analytical workflow. Therefore, we developed four types of bead-based mock communities as standard materials for microbiome analysis and evaluated potential experimental biases arising from nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and validation of four bead-based mock communities designed as quality control materials for clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing. The authors evaluated experimental biases from nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis, providing a standardized resource to improve reproducibility and quality in microbiome workflows.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into mechanisms of coral larval settlement induction and inhibition by marine biofilms.
papers.abstract: Biofilms are essential to larval settlement in many marine invertebrates, yet the mechanisms driving settlement induction or inhibition in corals remain poorly resolved. This challenge lies in the vast taxonomic and functional diversity of marine biofilms, making it difficult to identify cues associated with settlement. To address this, we analysed the metagenomes of biofilms used to induce settlement (attachment and metamorphosis) of four broadcast-spawning non-acroporid coral species: Dipsastrea favus, Platygyra sinensis, Echinophyllia aspera and Porites lobata. Biofilms were developed for o
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to investigate how marine biofilms induce or inhibit coral larval settlement, identifying functional and taxonomic features of biofilms associated with settlement of four broadcast-spawning coral species. The findings provide insights into the microbial cues and mechanisms underlying coral recruitment, which is critical for reef restoration efforts.

papers.title: Natural Infection of Domestic Dogs with Raccoon Dog and Fox Amdoparvovirus During a Severe Disease Outbreak.
papers.abstract: Raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV) has been reported in raccoon dogs and foxes, but natural infection in domestic dogs has not previously been documented. During March-April 2026, samples from four affected Dobermann dogs from a kennel near Novi Sad, Serbia, were submitted for laboratory investigation. After negative testing for canine adenovirus, canine coronavirus, herpesvirus, parvovirus, distemper virus, influenza A virus, and leptospirosis, metagenomic sequencing was performed on selected tissues, followed by bioinformatic analysis and targeted RFAV PCR screening of additional outb
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study documents the first natural infection of domestic dogs with raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV), identified during a severe disease outbreak in a Serbian kennel. Metagenomic sequencing and targeted PCR confirmed RFAV in affected Dobermanns after common canine pathogens were ruled out, highlighting a potential emerging pathogen in dogs.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein embeddings and genomic-neighborhood context to predict missing functional annotations for carbohydrate metabolism genes in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 silage metagenomes, CAAC achieved high cross-validation performance and improved annotation coverage, enabling more complete metabolic interpretation.

papers.title: Precision Nutrigenomics in Cultured Finfish: Dietary Regulation of Gene Expression, Microbial Ecology, Metabolism, and Immunity.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrigenomics requires a diet-microbiome-host perspective because microorganisms can transform feed substrates, generate bioactive metabolites, compete with pathogens, and modify intestinal and systemic gene regulation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative controlled feeding trials, transcriptomic and targeted gene-expression studies, microbiome analyses, and complementary multi-omic evidence concerning dietary regulations in cultured finfish. The available evidence is concentrated particularly on soybean-derived proteins, lipid-source replacements, selected am
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on precision nutrigenomics in farmed finfish, emphasizing the diet-microbiome-host axis and how dietary components like soybean proteins and lipid replacements regulate gene expression, microbial ecology, metabolism, and immunity. It highlights the need for integrated multi-omic approaches to optimize aquaculture diets.

papers.title: Gut Microbiome Composition Is Associated With Response to CD38 Antibody (Daratumumab) Treatment Among Relapsed Multiple Myeloma Patients.
papers.abstract: Growing data support interactions between host-gut microbes and treatment responses in multiple myeloma (MM), where a higher abundance of Eubacterium hallii in stool samples has been found among MM patients with negative minimal residual disease after induction therapy. Here, we evaluated changes in the gut microbiome associated with daratumumab (dara) based therapy in 40 MM patients, before and after therapy.
papers.summary: This study investigated how the gut microbiome changes in 40 relapsed multiple myeloma patients receiving daratumumab-based therapy. The findings suggest that gut microbiome composition is associated with treatment response, potentially linking specific microbial abundances to therapy outcomes.

papers.title: A hybrid and cost-efficient barcoding strategy for full-length 16S rRNA gene nanopore sequencing of environmental samples.
papers.abstract: Accurate species-level identification of bacteria in complex environmental samples is essential for applications in biotechnology, ecological monitoring, and clinical diagnostics. Short-read platforms such as Illumina frequently truncate the 16S rRNA gene, limiting taxonomic resolution. In this work, we applied Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) long-read sequencing to full-length 16S rRNA amplicon in samples from natural soil amended with lignocellulosic biomass and a simplified microbial community derived from cultures grown on selective and differential carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC)-based sub
papers.summary: This paper presents a hybrid barcoding strategy that combines short-read and long-read approaches to enable cost-efficient full-length 16S rRNA gene nanopore sequencing of environmental samples, improving species-level taxonomic resolution compared to short-read-only methods. The approach was validated on soil and simplified microbial community samples, demonstrating its utility for accurate bacterial identification in complex ecosystems.

papers.title: A Pan-European Whole-Microbiome Study of Wastewater Influent: Prokaryotes, Protists, Fungi, and Metazoa.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities entering wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) through untreated sewage represent an important interface between human, environmental, and treatment-associated microbiomes, yet our understanding of their biogeography remains poorly resolved, particularly for microbial eukaryotes. Using shotgun metagenomic time-series data from influent samples of seven WWTPs across a European latitudinal gradient, we analyzed the taxonomic composition and dynamics of bacteria, protists, fungi, and microscopic metazoa. Influent community composition varied with geographic location and season
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomic time-series data from seven wastewater treatment plants across a European latitudinal gradient to characterize the taxonomic composition and dynamics of bacteria, protists, fungi, and microscopic metazoa in untreated influent. The authors find that influent microbial community composition varies with geographic location and season, providing new insights into the biogeography of wastewater-associated microbial eukaryotes.

papers.title: Lesion-specific oral microbiome signatures and predicted carcinogenic pathways in oral squamous cell carcinoma: a paired-site study in Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma accounts for over 90% of oral neoplasms. Despite therapeutic advances, the lack of reliable, non-invasive biomarkers and delayed diagnosis continues to impede effective clinical management. By combining paired lesion and non-lesion sampling with predictive metagenomics analysis, our study addresses this gap and advances the current understanding of microbiome‒tumor interactions.
papers.summary: This study identifies distinct oral microbiome signatures at tumor sites compared to non-lesion sites in oral squamous cell carcinoma patients from Pakistan, using paired sampling and predictive metagenomics. The findings reveal lesion-specific bacterial communities and potential carcinogenic pathways, offering a step toward non-invasive biomarkers for early diagnosis.

papers.title: Ecological assembly of mucosal and fecal microbiomes in ulcerative colitis across genes, functions, and species.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with gut microbial dysbiosis, yet the ecological processes underlying community assembly remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how gut microbial communities assemble in ulcerative colitis patients by analyzing mucosal and fecal microbiomes across genes, functions, and species, revealing that ecological processes differ between these niches and are disrupted in disease. The findings provide insight into the dysbiosis associated with IBD, potentially informing future therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Multi-layer gut microbiome variation in type 2 diabetes despite preserved higher-order community structure.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) has been consistently associated with alterations in the gut microbiome, although disease, treatment, diet, and other host factors may contribute to the observed patterns. How these associations are organized across different biological levels of the microbial ecosystem remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates how type 2 diabetes (T2D) affects the gut microbiome across multiple biological levels, from individual taxa to higher-order community structure. Despite finding significant variation in taxonomic and functional layers associated with T2D, the overall higher-order community structure remained preserved, suggesting that disease-related shifts occur within a stable ecological framework.

papers.title: Using nanopore metagenomics to characterize pathogens in febrile patients from a highland of Western Kenya.
papers.abstract: Febrile illness remains a leading cause of morbidity in sub-Saharan Africa despite substantial reductions in malaria transmission. As malaria positive cases decrease, an increasing number of patients with febrile illnesses test negative for Plasmodium infection, leaving their causes unresolved. As a result of the diagnostic gap, patients receive presumptive antimalarial treatment, unnecessary antibiotics and experience delayed therapy.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore metagenomics to identify pathogens in febrile patients from a highland region of Western Kenya, aiming to address the diagnostic gap for non-malarial febrile illnesses. The approach demonstrates potential for characterizing causative agents, which could improve patient management and reduce inappropriate treatments.

papers.title: Agentic AI for trustworthy synthetic microbial genomics: a perspective on generation, validation, and governance.
papers.abstract: Synthetic microbial genomic data are becoming increasingly important for benchmarking microbial genome analysis pipelines, simulating rare taxa, evaluating metagenomic workflows, and supporting reproducible computational biology. Recent genomic foundation models demonstrate that biological sequences can be modelled at unprecedented scale, with emerging capacity for genome-level interpretation, generation, and design. However, the scientific value of synthetic microbial genomic data depends not only on whether sequences can be generated, but whether they are biologically plausible, computationa
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses how agentic AI could be used to generate, validate, and govern synthetic microbial genomic data, emphasizing the need for biological plausibility and trustworthy workflows. It highlights the potential of genomic foundation models for large-scale sequence generation while addressing challenges in ensuring data quality and governance.

papers.title: Microbial enzyme-responsive inulin nanoparticles for colon-targeted oral delivery of 5-ASA toward improved therapy of inflammatory bowel disease.
papers.abstract: Colon-targeted delivery of 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) offers an effective strategy for treating inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) while minimizing systemic side effects. However, conventional oral 5-ASA formulations suffer from premature drug release and poor colon specificity. To overcome these limitations, we developed a biodegradable, prebiotic, and immunomodulatory inulin nanoparticle (INP) platform enabling microbial enzyme-responsive and site-specific release of 5-ASA in the colon.
papers.summary: This paper describes a new colon-targeted oral drug delivery system using inulin nanoparticles that release 5-ASA in response to microbial enzymes in the colon, improving treatment of inflammatory bowel disease. The platform addresses limitations of conventional formulations by reducing premature release and enhancing colon specificity, while also leveraging inulin's prebiotic and immunomodulatory properties.

papers.title: Effect of quorum quenching enzyme YtnP on immune response and intestinal microbiota in Aeromonas hydrophila-infected grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella).
papers.abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila induces tissue swelling, necrosis, ulcers, and hemorrhagic septicemia in grass carp, causing significant economic losses. Quorum sensing, a communication mechanism among microorganisms, plays a key role in microbial ecological competition and dynamic equilibrium. Quorum quenching has emerged as a hot spot in anti-bacterial infection research. In this study, grass carp (n = 75 per group) were intraperitoneally injected with A. hydrophila and the quorum quenching enzyme YtnP. The expression levels of immune-related genes were assessed by qPCR. The intestinal microbiota was s
papers.summary: This study investigates the effects of the quorum quenching enzyme YtnP on immune responses and gut microbiota in grass carp infected with Aeromonas hydrophila. The findings suggest that YtnP modulates immune gene expression and intestinal microbial composition, potentially offering a strategy to combat bacterial infections in aquaculture.

papers.title: Exposure-aware multi-omics and artificial intelligence for biomarker discovery and precision prevention in diffuse glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse gliomas are now diagnosed and studied through integrated molecular classification, radiomics, single-cell biology, spatial profiling, proteogenomics, metabolomics, and artificial intelligence. Yet many precision-medicine models still begin at diagnosis and emphasize tumor-intrinsic molecular features, leaving environmental, occupational, lifestyle, microbiome, metabolic, immune, and treatment-related exposures at the margins. This review develops an exposome-informed view of diffuse glioma biomarker discovery. Biomarker discovery is separated from clinical prevention: current evidence
papers.summary: This review argues that diffuse glioma biomarker discovery and precision prevention should incorporate the exposome—environmental, occupational, lifestyle, microbiome, and treatment-related exposures—alongside tumor-intrinsic molecular data. It highlights how multi-omics and AI can integrate exposure data to improve biomarker discovery and prevention strategies, rather than focusing only on diagnosis and tumor features.

papers.title: Decoding the functional diversity of plant growth-promoting bacterial communities in the soils of Western Ghats, Tamil Nadu, India.
papers.abstract: Western ghats in India, one of the world's biodiversity hot spots is the reservoirs of microbial resources having agricultural and industrial significance. However, the diversity of plant growth-promoting microbial communities associated with the plants and soil in the Western Ghats is untapped vault. The current emphasis on natural farming is more depending on the indigenous microbial communities and their metabolic functions towards sustainable one -health. With this background, the present study examines the bacterial diversity of soils from the Western Ghats of Nilgiris, Coimbatore and Din
papers.summary: This study explores the bacterial diversity in soils from the Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot in India, focusing on plant growth-promoting bacteria. It highlights the untapped potential of these indigenous microbial communities for sustainable agriculture and one-health approaches.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites target C5AR1/KDM2A/HCAR3 axis in inflammatory bowel disease: a multi-machine learning algorithms and molecular docking study.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic recurrent disorder. Gut microbiota-derived metabolites regulate intestinal homeostasis, but their molecular mechanisms in IBD remain unclear. Current studies lack systematic "microbiota-metabolite-target" network mining with multi-method validation. This study integrates network pharmacology, three machine learning algorithms, and molecular docking to construct this regulatory network in IBD.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, multiple machine learning algorithms, and molecular docking to construct a 'gut microbiota-metabolite-target' regulatory network in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), identifying a C5AR1/KDM2A/HCAR3 axis as a potential key pathway. The findings suggest that gut microbiota-derived metabolites may influence IBD through this axis, providing a systematic framework for understanding the molecular mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Gut microbiota profiles and potential biomarkers in pre-pubertal females with ADHD.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder with significant sex differences in diagnostic rates; males being diagnosed more frequently than females. Gut microbiota alterations may contribute to ADHD via the microbiota-gut-brain axis. However, previous microbiota studies have predominantly used male or mixed-gender samples, neglecting females with distinct clinical and hormonal profiles. The pre-pubertal period is critical for both neurodevelopment and microbiota maturation. This study investigates gut microbiota characteristics in pre-pube
papers.summary: This study examines gut microbiota differences in pre-pubertal females with ADHD compared to controls, addressing a gap in research that has largely focused on males or mixed-gender cohorts. The authors identify potential microbial biomarkers associated with ADHD in this specific population, suggesting a role for the microbiota-gut-brain axis in females.

papers.title: Fighting the invader: strategies against intracellular bacteria.
papers.abstract: Intracellular pathogenic bacteria are often-overlooked agent of chronic, recurrent and difficult-to-treat infections in a context of escalating antimicrobial resistance. By hiding within professional and non-professional phagocytes, adopting dormant or slow-replicative states and rewiring host pathways, these pathogens successfully evade both immune clearance and conventional antibiotic therapy, thus contributing to treatment failure and, potentially, carcinogenesis. Here we synthesise how obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade and persist within host cells, and interpret these
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade and persist within host cells, highlighting their strategies to evade immune clearance and antibiotic therapy. It discusses the clinical challenges of chronic, recurrent infections and potential links to carcinogenesis, while outlining therapeutic approaches against these pathogens.

papers.title: Hormone priming and metabolic engineering of phytohormone crosstalk in rice under combined biotic and abiotic stresses: a multi-omics perspective for climate-resilient crop development.
papers.abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is the caloric backbone for more than half of humanity, yet it remains one of the most vulnerable crops to the simultaneous biotic and abiotic stresses exacerbated by climate change. Phytohormone priming and the complex crosstalk networks governed by transcription factor hubs like WRKY, MYB, and NAC serve as the central adaptive mechanism for stress resilience. This review synthesizes how multi-omics integration, including spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, is resolving the molecular architecture of hormonal priming and epigenetic stress memory. We critically evalu
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on how phytohormone priming and crosstalk networks (involving WRKY, MYB, and NAC transcription factors) mediate rice stress responses to combined biotic and abiotic stresses. It highlights how multi-omics approaches, including spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, are uncovering the molecular architecture of hormonal priming and epigenetic stress memory, offering a framework for engineering climate-resilient rice.

papers.title: Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 alleviates sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and enhancing S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) impairs cognitive function and induces hippocampal injury, yet the gut-derived mechanisms underlying these deficits remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study shows that the probiotic Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 can alleviate cognitive impairment caused by sleep deprivation in mice. The mechanism involves remodeling the gut microbiota and enhancing S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation, which helps protect hippocampal function.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration identifies a gut-microbiota-associated plasma metabolite signature for alzheimer disease diagnosis and metabolic pathway targeting.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia, with early diagnosis remaining constrained by the invasiveness and limited accessibility of current biomarkers. The gut-brain axis has emerged as a critical communication network linking intestinal homeostasis with central nervous system function, yet the diagnostic utility of gut-microbiota-associated circulating metabolites in AD remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to identify a plasma metabolite signature associated with gut microbiota that can aid in Alzheimer's disease diagnosis and reveal potential metabolic pathways for therapeutic targeting. The findings support the gut-brain axis's role in AD and suggest a non-invasive diagnostic approach.

papers.title: Probiotic mediated modulation of neonatal health: a meta-analysis of prematurity-related morbidity, jaundice, and respiratory distress.
papers.abstract: Prematurity remains a major contributor to neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with neonatal jaundice and respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) representing two of the most common complications associated with immature hepatic and pulmonary development. Increasing evidence suggests that probiotic supplementation may improve neonatal outcomes through modulation of the gut microbiome, gut-liver axis, and gut-lung axis; however, published findings remain inconsistent. The meta-analysis evaluated the effects of probiotic supplementation on prematurity-related morbidity, with particular empha
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This meta-analysis evaluates the effects of probiotic supplementation on neonatal complications associated with prematurity, including jaundice and respiratory distress syndrome. The findings suggest that probiotics may improve neonatal outcomes by modulating the gut microbiome and related axes, though results highlight variability across studies.

papers.title: Non-nutritive sweeteners, the gut microbiome, and tumor immunity: evidence hierarchy and a sucralose-centered translational model.
papers.abstract: Non-nutritive sweeteners (NNS) are widely used sugar substitutes and constitute heterogeneous dietary and non-dietary exposures. Human gut microbiota findings vary by sweetener identity, purified compound versus commercial formulation, carrier ingredients, dose, duration, host background, and analytical method. Purified compounds and commercial formulations are therefore biologically non-equivalent. A structured narrative search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection was conducted from database inception through 17 July 2026 without language restrictions. Evidence was organi
papers.summary: This review examines how non-nutritive sweeteners (NNS), particularly sucralose, affect the gut microbiome and tumor immunity, highlighting that purified compounds and commercial formulations are biologically non-equivalent due to carrier ingredients and other factors. The authors propose a sucralose-centered translational model and organize evidence hierarchically to guide future research on NNS-microbiome-immune interactions.

papers.title: Time-dependent shifts in microbiota and metabolites of Yuba under ambient storage: implication for quality deterioration and spoilage.
papers.abstract: Yuba (tofu skin), a high-protein and high-lipid plant-based food, is prone to spoilage at ambient temperatures, but the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to elucidate the dynamic changes in the microbial community and metabolites of Yuba during ambient storage to investigate quality deterioration and identify potential biomarkers for quality control.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the microbial community and metabolites of Yuba (tofu skin) change over time during ambient storage, revealing dynamic shifts that contribute to quality deterioration and spoilage. The findings identify potential biomarkers that could be used for quality control of this high-protein, high-lipid plant-based food.

papers.title: Fermented fruit waste as a microbiome-active soil amendment: a review of field and greenhouse evidence (2009-2025).
papers.abstract: Fruit residues generated across the global food supply chain constitute a rapidly growing, biologically reactive waste stream that, when left unmanaged, degrades environmental and agricultural quality, whereas controlled microbial fermentation offers a practical means of transforming this waste into stabilized, biologically active soil amendments. This review synthesizes evidence from field trials, greenhouse experiments, and microbiome studies published between 2009 and 2025 to evaluate the agronomic and microbiome-level effects of fermented fruit waste (FFW) as a soil amendment within circul
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from 2009-2025 on using fermented fruit waste as a soil amendment, showing it can improve soil microbiome activity and agronomic outcomes while managing agricultural waste. It highlights the potential of controlled fermentation to convert fruit residues into stabilized, biologically active products that benefit soil health.

papers.title: Association between gut microbiota characteristics and therapeutic efficacy of multimodal combination therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus: a secondary analysis of a prospective phase II trial.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) carries a poor prognosis. Although SBRT combined with cadonilimab and lenvatinib has shown encouraging antitumor activity in a prior prospective phase II trial, marked interpatient heterogeneity remains. Gut microbiota may influence antitumor immunity and could help identify patients more or less likely to benefit from this regimen.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiota composition is associated with the efficacy of a multimodal combination therapy (SBRT plus cadonilimab and lenvatinib) in hepatocellular carcinoma patients with portal vein tumor thrombus. By analyzing samples from a prospective phase II trial, the authors identify specific microbial features that may predict therapeutic response, suggesting gut microbiota as a potential biomarker for patient stratification in this challenging setting.
